newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean troops pull back towards Bukavu, witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Zairean troops pull back towards Bukavu, witnesses.

text.p: Frightened Zairean troops pulled back towards the South Kivu provincial capital of Bukavu on Thursday as refugees straggled to a camp to the northwest, witnesses said.
Reuters photographer Corinne Dufka said she saw about 150 Zairean paratroops, militiamen and refugee camp guards on a road half way between Bukavu and Nyangezi town, 27 km (17 miles) to the south.
"They were jumping on any passing car and leaving towards Bukavu. They looked very rag-tag. They were anxious and very irritable. A militiamen even tried to steal our car," Dufka said.
"We also saw a couple of wounded soldiers on the road," she added.
She said about 1,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees from camps to the south were straggling along the road towards Nyamiragwe camp northwest of Bukavu fearful of rebel advances.

Aid workers said the Zairean army told U.N. aid agencies on Thursday that between 10 and 15 members of the Zairean contingent charged with guarding refugee camps were taken hostage on Wednesday at a hilltop camp near Nyangezi town.
Aid officials said Zairean troops confiscated two aid agency vehicles in Bukavu city on Thursday. Dufka said traffic south of the city was light as civilians feared their cars would also be taken.
Zairean soldiers set up roadblocks on Thursday in Bukavu and controlled movements of people. Officers said they expected heavy reinforcements to arrive from the capital Kinshasa on Thursday.
Aid workers said ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge fighters reached Nyangezi on Wednesday night. It was not clear if the town had fallen and the army stopped Reuters journalists driving there on Thursday.
Unconfirmed reports from Zairean soldiers said Banyamulenge had also seized Kamanyola and Bwegera towns, south of Bukavu.
